subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group: cross-agent sessions_list visibility mismatch causes one-way sessions_send failure

question: Should same Telegram group membership make two configured agents mutually visible/sendable, or should cross-agent `sessions_send` remain governed only by explicit session visibility and A2A policy controls?
rationale: The code path is clear, but changing it decides a cross-agent session authorization boundary and could expose metadata or transcript access if handled as an implicit group trust rule.

options.title: Require explicit policy and live proof
options.body: Keep same-group membership non-authoritative by itself, then fix only through an approved A2A/per-capability/per-agent policy shape with tests proving list/history/status isolation and live Telegram A/B send proof.

options.title: Fold into generic A2A-send work
options.body: Treat the remaining send failure as part of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57447 while keeping this issue for Telegram-specific reproduction evidence until that fix proves this case.

options.title: Accept same-group implicit trust
options.body: Allow agents in the same Telegram group to discover and send to each other, accepting the need for a new explicit security contract and documentation.

recommendation.title: Require explicit policy and live proof
recommendation.body: Keep same-group membership non-authoritative by itself, then fix only through an approved A2A/per-capability/per-agent policy shape with tests proving list/history/status isolation and live Telegram A/B send proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The central history points to prior session access/scoping work by this handle, and the unresolved choice is a product/security boundary decision on that surface.
